reviewerSelfCorrection: This is the second consecutive version where Codex found a blocker I did not. HAE7-CX-01 is real and I confirmed it from v7's own bytes before looking at v8: v7's actionClass closedValues were CA-1-HOST-HEAD, CA-2, CA-3, CA-4-HOST, while targetIdentity's union branches keyed on CA-1 and CA-2 and its own nullWhen keyed on 'CA-3 and CA-4-HOST', and byteCap's variants keyed on 'CA-1 or CA-2', 'CA-4-HOST' and 'CA-3'. A single member therefore mixed two vocabularies, and a validator resolving when: CA-1 against a record whose actionClass is CA-1-HOST-HEAD would match no branch, so the CA-1 target-identity branch could never select. At v7 I verified the member types, the forbidden-shape lists, the per-class grounding against doctor v4, and a six-region byte-identity diff, and I did not check that the discriminator predicates were drawn from one domain. Method note, recorded because it is the same lesson twice: at v7 I applied the prior round's finding as a class and swept every scope member for open objects, which was right, but I swept only for the defect already named. This round I checked predicate-domain consistency mechanically across the whole shape rather than reading the three sites the prompt names.
summary: The repair is exactly what the prompt specifies and it is verifiable rather than asserted. A new classPredicateDomain block fixes one discriminator domain — doctor-v4 consentRecords[].actionClass with closedValues CA-1 through CA-4 — supplies a translation from the authorization-record labels, and states the rule that authorization-record labels do not appear as scope predicates. I tested that claim mechanically instead of accepting it: stripping the translation block itself, CA-1-HOST-HEAD and CA-4-HOST occur zero times in the shape body, and every class predicate remaining is drawn from the four-value domain. The translation is total over the four record labels, injective, and its targets exactly equal the domain's closed values. The CA-4 send and receive variant now actually selects, because its predicate finally matches the domain it is evaluated in. The updated FC-BOUND-SHAPE fixture adds the exhaustiveness property that makes the v7 defect non-recurrable: 'No legal serialized class is unmatched.' Six regions are byte-identical to v7, so no preview-denial or fail-closed regression is possible, and the global change set is confined to the discriminator repair, one fixture, the accounting and the version bump.

predecessorFindingVerification.HAE7-CX-01: REPAIRED (repair present; original finding text unseen, though I confirmed the underlying defect independently from v7's bytes as recorded at reviewerSelfCorrection). v8 adds consentRecordsScopeShape.classPredicateDomain with four parts: domain 'doctor-v4 consentRecords[].actionClass'; closedValues CA-1, CA-2, CA-3, CA-4; translationFromAuthorizationRecord mapping CA-1-HOST-HEAD to CA-1, CA-2 to CA-2, CA-3 to CA-3 and CA-4-HOST to CA-4; and the rule 'Every conditional in this scope shape is evaluated against the serialized doctor-v4 actionClass after that translation. Authorization-record labels CA-1-HOST-HEAD and CA-4-HOST do not appear as scope predicates.' The three mixed predicates are corrected in place: targetIdentity.nullWhen moves from 'CA-3 and CA-4-HOST' to 'CA-3 and CA-4', and byteCap's second variant moves from when CA-4-HOST to when CA-4. The authorization-record actionClass closedValues are deliberately unchanged, which is correct — the record keeps its own labels and the translation carries them into the serialized domain, rather than the record being rewritten to match doctor.
predecessorFindingVerification.IR-HEA7 (none raised): I raised no finding on v7. The gap that produced Codex's blocker is recorded at reviewerSelfCorrection rather than presented here as a repaired finding of mine, because it was not mine.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 2cbad5612e546d3bf915074a8ad3fc4cae444122c997e2ddb3fe067d3cd022dc both times. No drift.

No mixed predicate domains remain, tested mechanically. I stripped the classPredicateDomain block — which must name the record labels in order to translate them — and swept the remaining shape body: CA-1-HOST-HEAD occurs zero times and CA-4-HOST occurs zero times. I then extracted every when, nullWhen, requiredWhen and mustBeNull predicate in the shape. The class predicates are CA-2 only, 'CA-3 and CA-4', CA-1, CA-2, 'CA-1 or CA-2', CA-4, CA-3 and CA-4 — every one inside the four-value domain. The single non-class predicate is policyProvenance's nullWhen 'invocation-time-naming', which is a consent-carrier condition rather than a class discriminator and is legitimately outside the domain.

The translation is well-formed as a function, not merely present. It is total over the authorization record's four actionClass closedValues, injective, and the set of its targets is exactly the domain's closedValues. So every legal record label maps to exactly one serialized class and no domain value is unreachable.

Exhaustiveness holds for both discriminated members against the four-value domain. byteCap variants cover CA-1 and CA-2 jointly, CA-4, and CA-3 — all four. targetIdentity covers CA-1 and CA-2 as union branches and CA-3 and CA-4 through nullWhen — all four. No legal class falls through either member, which is the property whose absence made the v7 defect bite.

CA-4 send and receive is no longer unselected. The variant retains closedMembers send and receive, both nonnegative-integer, with swappedOrMissingDirection 'fails', and its predicate is now CA-4, which matches the domain the shape says conditionals are evaluated in. In v7 that variant keyed on CA-4-HOST and so could never select against a serialized doctor record.

The fixture was strengthened rather than merely renamed. FC-BOUND-SHAPE now opens 'Parent consentRecords[].actionClass is the discriminator', enumerates which class selects which variant, and adds 'No legal serialized class is unmatched' alongside the previous rejection list. That is the fixture-level statement of the exhaustiveness property, so the v7 failure mode is testable rather than only fixed.

No deadline or byteCap shape regression. observationDeadline retains kind closed to DURATION-FROM-INVOCATION-START, clockRule closed to OBSERVATION-ONLY, and the forbiddenShapes list naming ISO-8601 instant, wall-clock expiry, empty object, bare number and string duration. byteCap retains its closed variants, the bytes unit, the nonnegative-integer rule and its forbidden-shape list.

No preview-denial or fail-closed regression, verified structurally. I flattened both documents and diffed six regions — failClosed, coveredActs, slice1EgressExecutionSide, joinBlockerDisposition, outcomeVocabulary and effectCommit. All six returned zero changed, zero added and zero removed paths, so the six-conjunct fail-closed rule, the CA-2 whole-class preview denial, the CA-1 IN_PROCESS denial, the egress split, the seven join-blocker dispositions, the closed outcome vocabulary and the four commit boundaries are byte-identical to what I reviewed at v7.

The change set is confined to the repair: globally 171 added, 149 removed and 9 changed paths, of which authorizationRecord accounts for 10 added and 3 changed (the classPredicateDomain block and the three predicate strings), acceptanceEvidenceFixtureClasses 1 changed (FC-BOUND-SHAPE), predecessorVerdictFindings 158 added and 149 removed (accounting), recordedInputs 3 added, and five header fields changed for the version bump. Nothing else moved.
No silent SATISFIED: the token occurs twice, both negative. Header retains CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, DO-NOT-SEAL and binds NOTHING.
No minted PT token: 'PT-' occurs eleven times, nine PT-NET-EGRESS and two the literal wildcard in the disclaimer. 'WAIV' occurs zero times.

verdictNote: ACCEPT, zero findings. The repair is the kind that is checkable rather than assertable: the artifact states a rule about its own predicates and I tested the rule against its own bytes, finding zero occurrences of either authorization-record label anywhere in the shape body once the translation block is set aside. I also checked the two properties the rule does not itself claim — that the translation is a total injective function onto the domain, and that both discriminated members are exhaustive over all four domain values — and both hold, which is what makes the v7 failure mode impossible rather than merely absent. The fixture now carries the exhaustiveness property explicitly. I have recorded, for the second consecutive round, a blocker I did not find, along with the method change it argues for. The acceptanceScope block is carried forward so this verdict is not read as sealing, applying, recording, or discharging anything.
